description: Source file implementing command line flag parsing and help message generation for the quiche project, including flag registration, setting, resetting, and help display functions.

classes.name: QuicheFlagRegistry
classes.description: Singleton class managing registration, setting, resetting, and help message generation for command line flags.

classes.name: QuicheParseCommandLineFlagsResult
classes.description: Structure holding the result of parsing command line flags, including non-flag arguments and optional exit status.

methods.name: FindLineWrapPosition
methods.description: Finds position to wrap a line based on whitespace within a string.

methods.name: AppendFlagDescription
methods.description: Formats and appends a command line flag description with proper wrapping.

methods.name: ToQuicheStringVector
methods.description: Converts vectors of strings or wide strings to ASCII string vectors, platform-specific overload.

methods.name: GetInstance
methods.description: Returns the singleton instance of QuicheFlagRegistry.

methods.name: RegisterFlag
methods.description: Registers a new command line flag with its helper.

methods.name: SetFlags
methods.description: Sets flags based on command line switches, returns success or failure.

methods.name: ResetFlags
methods.description: Resets all registered flags to default values.

methods.name: GetHelp
methods.description: Generates help message string for all registered flags.

methods.name: SetFlag
methods.description: Template specializations for setting flag values from strings for bool, uint16_t, int32_t, and std::string types.

methods.name: QuicheParseCommandLineFlagsImpl
methods.description: Initializes command line parsing, processes flags, and returns non-flag arguments.

methods.name: QuicheParseCommandLineFlagsHelper
methods.description: Parses command line, handles help flag, sets flags, and determines exit status.

methods.name: QuichePrintCommandLineFlagHelpImpl
methods.description: Prints usage and help message for command line flags.
